title: Structural hashing (AST-based, whitespace/comment-invariant)
description:
Replace blake3-over-raw-text hashing in symbol_diff.rs with AST-token-stream hashing that ignores whitespace and comments. Currently sutra's `signature_hash` and `body_hash` are blake3 over raw extracted text — reformatting registers as SignatureChanged/BodyChanged even with zero semantic change.

sem's approach (MIT, can port directly with attribution): zero-alloc AST token stream through xxHash64, skipping comment nodes, normalizing whitespace via `trim_bytes`, hashing both node *kind* (structure) and leaf *text* (content). Also has a variant that excludes the entity's own name span so a bare rename yields the same structural hash — prerequisite for rename detection (task 2).

This is the highest-priority item because it directly improves diff quality AND is the foundation for rename/move detection.

Reference implementation:
- `sutra-surveys/sem/crates/sem-core/src/utils/hash.rs` — `structural_hash()`, `hash_structural_tokens()`, `structural_hash_excluding_range()`
- `sutra-surveys/sem/crates/sem-core/src/model/entity.rs` — `SemanticEntity.structural_hash` field

Sutra integration points:
- `sutra/src/tools/symbol_diff.rs` — where `signature_hash` / body hash comparisons drive Added/Deleted/SignatureChanged/BodyChanged classification
- `sutra/src/parser/{rust,dart,c,python}.rs` — where `ExtractedSymbol` is produced; `signature_hash` is currently blake3 of the signature string

License: sem is MIT. Direct port into AGPL sutra is fine — add attribution in NOTICE file.

decisions.decision: xxh3-64 (new xxhash-rust dep) over existing blake3
decisions.rationale: Faithful port of sem's streaming zero-alloc traversal; 64-bit collision risk irrelevant at repo scale
decisions.rejected: blake3 (already a dep) — streaming works but re-deriving the traversal against a different hasher invites port-divergence bugs for no benefit

decisions.decision: Single name-span-excluded structural hash serves both cosmetic-change detection and rename matching
decisions.rationale: For cosmetic detection the matched pair has identical names, so name exclusion is harmless; sem's phase-2 rename matching requires the exclusion
decisions.rejected: Dual variants (name-included + name-excluded) — redundant storage and compute

decisions.decision: Persist structural_hash as nullable symbols-table column now
decisions.rationale: Trivial migration (nullable, upsert-backfilled on reindex); unlocks incremental-reindex skip and sutra_similar/duplicates reuse later
decisions.rejected: Diff-path-only computation — avoids migration but forecloses reuse; migration cost is near zero

decisions.decision: CosmeticChanged as explicit new ChangeKind, weighted ~0 in consumers
decisions.rationale: Sutra consumers surface change lists; silently collapsing to unchanged loses information and violates refactor contract discipline (L9)
decisions.rejected: sem's behavior (drop the match entirely, report nothing)

implementation_plan:
Design settled 2026-07-10 (exploration + grilling in session). Corrections to original description: sutra's signature_hash is blake3 over a CONSTRUCTED signature string (build_fn_signature), computed at parse time while the tree-sitter node is alive — no plumbing problem. The raw-text hash is body_hash, computed post-hoc in symbol_diff.rs. The diff path (diff_file, symbol_diff.rs:164-212) re-parses both git blobs fresh and never reads the persisted index, so the diff use case itself needs no migration.

Plan:
1. Add xxhash-rust (xxh3) dep. Port sem's hash_structural_tokens + excluding-range variant from /home/josh/soft/sutra-surveys/sem/crates/sem-core/src/utils/hash.rs into new src/parser/structural_hash.rs — language-agnostic fn(node: &Node, source: &[u8], exclude: Option<Range<usize>>) -> u64, formatted "{:016x}". Iterative pre-order DFS with reused TreeCursor + reversed-children worklist; skip comment kinds {comment, line_comment, block_comment, doc_comment, tag_comment}; leaf nodes → ASCII-trimmed byte slice + b" "; internal nodes → kind bytes + b":". Excluding variant skips leaves overlapping the excluded byte range, still descends internals. MIT attribution in NOTICE file.
2. Compute ONE hash per symbol: name-span-excluded structural hash (exclude = the symbol's own name node byte range). Compute inside extract_symbol() in each of src/parser/{rust,dart,c,python}.rs where signature_hash is already computed (node alive). New field structural_hash: Option<String> on ExtractedSymbol (parser/mod.rs:22-40).
3. Persist: new migration adding nullable structural_hash column to symbols table; wire through InsertSymbolParams/SymbolRow (db/mod.rs:233-262) and the upsert (db/mod.rs:790-891, structural_hash = excluded.structural_hash). Old rows NULL until reindex — no backfill needed.
4. symbol_diff.rs classify_symbols: for matched pairs where signature_hash equal and body_hash (raw text) differs, compare structural hashes; equal → new ChangeKind::CosmeticChanged (formatting/comment-only). Otherwise BodyChanged as today.
5. diff_impact.rs: serialize CosmeticChanged; audit so cosmetic changes carry ~zero weight in any counting/risk aggregation (contract change: BodyChanged counts will drop — this is the point, but per lessons ledger L9 discipline, diff the behavioral contract of every consumer).

Tests: reformat-only fixture → CosmeticChanged; comment-only edit → CosmeticChanged; real body change → BodyChanged; two symbols differing only in name → equal structural hashes (foundation for sutra/227); per-language coverage rust+dart minimum.
execution_record: Implemented as planned with minor divergences: (1) Migration 0047 marked ephemeral_only=true because the symbols table itself is ephemeral — on reindex, the table is dropped and recreated from 0001_initial, so the ALTER TABLE must re-run. (2) For C parser, added find_name_node_in_declarator helper (mirrors existing find_name_in_declarator but returns Node instead of String) to get the name byte range for deeply-nested declarator chains. (3) Dart's build_symbol takes structural_hash as a parameter (same pattern as signature/signature_hash) since the name node comes from different source nodes (sig_node vs span_node) depending on the extraction path.

messages.text:
Codex review: approve with notes (3 medium findings).

1. NULL structural_hash after non-reindex upgrade — by design per plan (diff path re-parses fresh, doesn't read DB). DB consumers need reparse.
2. C/Python not in language_for_path — pre-existing limitation, not a regression from this task.
3. C field hashes excluded name incorrectly (passed None) — FIXED in 8819bbc. find_field_identifier refactored to return Node for byte-range exclusion.

edges.note: Rename detection requires structural hashing to match entities by AST structure excluding name span
